explicit_detail: Mark names Jairus as a synagogue ruler and says his little daughter is at the point of death when he appeals to Jesus.
sequence_boundary: Matthew does not name Jairus in its parallel.

explicit_detail: Mark says the woman suffered under many physicians, spent all she had, and became worse before touching Jesus' clothing.

explicit_detail: Jesus perceives that power has gone out from him and asks who touched his clothes; the woman comes fearing and trembling and tells the truth.

explicit_detail: Mark records the Aramaic 'Talitha cumi', says the girl was twelve, and notes she rose and walked; Jesus orders food for her.

explicit_detail: Luke names Jairus, identifies him as a synagogue ruler, and says he had an only daughter about twelve years old who was dying.
sequence_boundary: Mark says little daughter near death; Luke uniquely says only daughter in this scope.

explicit_detail: Luke says the woman had a twelve-year discharge of blood and could not be healed by anyone.

speaker: Narrator

explicit_detail: Luke says the girl's spirit returned; she rose immediately, and Jesus directed that she be given something to eat.

explicit_detail: John 4 narrates a different healing involving a royal official's son who was sick at Capernaum while Jesus was in Cana.

explicit_detail: The servants meet the official and report that the child lives; the father learns the fever left at the hour Jesus spoke.
